heading: Phase 1 UI rework — A4 ProductCover system
text:
Phase 1 UI rework — A4 ProductCover system

- Date: 2026-05-24
- Status: Done
- Branch: feature/phase1-customer-frontend
- TaskMaster tag: phase1-customer-frontend (no TaskMaster ID — UI rework continues under docs/phase1-ui-redesign.md)
- Scope: Fourth step of the Phase 1 customer frontend UI rework. Ships the programmatic product-cover system — a pure-function spec resolver (utils/cover.ts), a thin SVG renderer (components/ProductCover.vue), and a Vitest spec covering determinism + edge cases. The backend product API does not return any image URL, and we are forbidden from changing it, so every product visual in the storefront has to be generated client-side. The contract is: given a productId (and optionally a name), the resolver returns a fully-deterministic CoverSpec — same inputs ALWAYS produce the same palette, geometry, rotation, offset, and initial mark — so the same product looks identical on the list card, the detail hero, the order row, and the checkout summary. No view imports ProductCover yet (B1 will be the first consumer), so this commit produces ZERO visual change on every customer-facing page.
- Implemented:
  - NEW frontend/src/utils/cover.ts (~115 lines) — three exports: fnv1a(str) returns a 32-bit unsigned FNV-1a hash via Math.imul (10 lines, no deps); extractInitial(name) walks the trimmed string char-by-char with a CJK Unified Ideographs (main + Extension A) + CJK Compatibility Ideographs regex and returns the first CJK glyph it finds, falling back to up to 2 alphanumeric chars uppercased after stripping non-alphanumerics, and falling back to '?' for empty/whitespace/non-alphanumeric input; coverFor(productId, name) hashes `${productId}::${name}` and uses different bit-ranges of the hash to pick palette (hash % 8), geometry (hash>>>8 % 6), rotation in 15° steps (hash>>>16 % 24 × 15), and two small offsets in [-0.2, 0.2] (different 8-bit windows mapped through (b/255 - 0.5) × 0.4). The seed itself is exposed on the returned spec so the SVG renderer can build stable `<defs>` ids without an instance counter — same product → same gradient id → no DOM duplication noise.
  - NEW frontend/src/components/ProductCover.vue (~210 lines) — `<ProductCover :productId :name :aspect :grade :size />`. Computes the spec via coverFor, then renders an inline SVG with three layers: (1) a vertical linearGradient base (palette.base → palette.baseDark); (2) a single geometry primitive rendered inside `<g transform="rotate(θ cx cy)">` where the primitive type is determined by spec.geometry — disc (large circle, 0.36 × major axis radius), arc (half-circle path from -0.42 to +0.42), lines (3 horizontal rectangles at y offsets -0.18 / -0.02 / +0.14), rings (3 concentric stroke-only circles at radii 0.4 / 0.28 / 0.16), diamond (rotated 56% × 56% square, additional rotate(45) on top of the spec rotation), composite (a triangle + a small filled circle in accentDeep); (3) a bottom-left initial mark in Inter Tight 700 at 18% of viewBox height, accentDeep color, 0.92 opacity. When grade='detail' two extra layers stack on top: a radial halo gradient at the top-right (accent at 0.2 opacity fading to 0% over 60% radius) and an feTurbulence fractalNoise filter at 0.05 alpha matrix giving the cover detail-grade tactile texture for the product detail hero. The figure element gets its dimensions from a size prop (sm 64 / md 160 / lg 280 / full 100%) combined with a CSS aspect-ratio derived from aspect (4:5 / 1:1 / 16:9), so the cover always preserves its proportion regardless of container width. preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" + the explicit aspect-ratio together prevent any letterboxing.
  - NEW frontend/src/utils/__tests__/cover.spec.ts (~110 lines, 17 tests across 3 describe blocks) — fnv1a: determinism for the same input including a CJK example, distinct-output for different inputs, range check (unsigned 32-bit integer) over 5 sample strings; extractInitial: first CJK glyph including mid-string CJK ("Premium 茶具 set" → "茶"), Latin uppercased slice (aroma → AR, a → A), non-alphanumeric stripped before slicing (3-pack → 3P, !!premium → PR), all four nullish/empty fallbacks return '?'; coverFor: deterministic same-input round-trip including a CJK product name, numeric and string productId yield identical spec (so the caller doesn't need to .toString()), 100-sample sweeps confirm palette ∈ PALETTES and geometry ∈ GEOMETRIES, rotation is always a multiple of 15 in [0, 360), offsets always within [-0.2, 0.2], null/undefined/empty inputs don't throw, different productIds OR different names yield distinct seeds, initial wiring (CJK → first glyph, latin → 2 uppercased, empty → '?').
  - APPENDED docs/dev-log.md (this entry).
- Decisions and trade-offs:
  - FNV-1a was picked over djb2 or a CRC variant because it's (a) trivial to write in 10 lines without lookup tables, (b) produces good distribution across the 8-palette × 6-geometry × 24-rotation × 256-offset space we actually use, and (c) is stable across Node, browsers, and any future SSR runtime. We don't need cryptographic strength here — just stable per-product visual identity.
  - The hash input is `${idStr}::${nameStr}` rather than just `${idStr}` so that two products with the same numeric id but different names (which shouldn't happen in production but could in test fixtures) get distinct visuals. The `::` separator prevents ambiguity between e.g. (id="1", name="2A") and (id="12", name="A"). The name still primarily feeds the initial mark; its contribution to the hash is incidental.
  - The 6 geometries are intentionally abstract — no realistic product silhouettes (no candle shapes, no bottle outlines, etc.). The brief calls for a boutique-magazine feel, not an icon library. Customers immediately learn that the cover is a stylized visual signature for the product, not a photo, which sidesteps the entire "this looks like a placeholder" failure mode that fake product icons would create.
  - The initial mark sits at the bottom-left (0.08 × w, 0.92 × h) rather than centered, because a centered mark fights with the geometry layer for focal weight; the corner placement reads as a signed-print maker's mark and lets the geometry breathe. accentDeep was chosen over accent for the text fill because the deeper shade reads more clearly over the lighter geometry shapes when they happen to overlap the text area.
  - Detail-grade is opt-in via grade='detail', not derived from size or aspect. The cost is a turbulence filter (which is GPU-rasterized but non-trivial) plus an extra radial gradient. We only want to pay that cost on the product detail hero, not on a 30-card list view or a 32px order-row thumbnail — even though all three use the same component.
  - SVG ids are derived from spec.seed (e.g. `pcv-grad-${seed}`). Two ProductCover instances of the same product on the same page will produce identical id strings — that's intentional and correct, because the referenced `<linearGradient>` definitions are literally the same definition. SVG `url(#id)` reference resolves to the first matching element in the document, which works fine in this case. Different products will produce different ids because their seeds differ.
  - Component lives at components/ root level (NOT components/atoms/) because it's a molecule, not an atom — it composes the cover spec with SVG geometry logic and grade-conditional layers. The atom subfolder is reserved for pure-presentation primitives (Button, Pill, Skeleton, etc.) with no business logic. ProductCover's coverFor call qualifies as light business logic (deterministic visual identity per product), so it belongs at the molecule level alongside future ProductCard, OrderCard, etc.
  - No Vitest tests for the ProductCover.vue render output itself were added. The render is purely a function of the CoverSpec (which IS tested), and DOM-snapshot tests for SVG are brittle (whitespace, attribute order). The visual contract gets validated by the consuming-view tests in Phase B (e.g. B1's ProductCard.spec) and by manual visual smoke once a view actually mounts it.
- Changed files: NEW frontend/src/utils/cover.ts; NEW frontend/src/components/ProductCover.vue; NEW frontend/src/utils/__tests__/cover.spec.ts; docs/dev-log.md (this entry). Zero modifications to existing files.
- Commands run: `git status` + `git log --oneline -5` at start (clean, HEAD c13a2db A3); `ls frontend/src/utils/` + `ls frontend/src/components/atoms/` + `ls frontend/src/components/__tests__/` to confirm file locations; `cat frontend/vite.config.ts` to confirm the vitest include glob picks up `src/**/*.{test,spec}.ts` (so src/utils/__tests__/cover.spec.ts auto-discovers); `mkdir -p frontend/src/utils/__tests__`; `npx vitest run` (4 spec files / 33 tests pass, ~1.05s — PaymentView 4 + CheckoutView 5 + QuantityStepper 7 + cover 17 new); `npm run build` (vue-tsc --noEmit + vite build, exit 0, 3.86s); chunk-size diff vs A3 (c13a2db) verified — main bundle and every view chunk byte-identical.
- Test result: 33/33 vitest tests pass (was 16/16 before A4; +17 from cover.spec.ts) in ~1.05s, no flakes — including the determinism round-trip, the 100-sample palette/geometry/rotation/offset sweeps, the numeric-vs-string id equivalence, and the empty/null edge cases. `npm run build` clean. Build deltas vs A3 (commit c13a2db): main bundle index-T-gHTfFy.js stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL at 1086.56 kB (utils/cover.ts is a small pure-function module and ProductCover.vue is a single-file component; both are fully tree-shaken because no view imports them yet); ALL 8 lazy view chunks byte-identical (LoginView 2.31, RegisterView 3.55, ProductListView 3.69, OrdersView 4.57, OrderDetailView 5.41, ProductDetailView 5.87, CheckoutView 6.64, PaymentView 9.27 kB); index CSS unchanged at 369.34 kB. No type errors. The pre-existing Element Plus full-import >500 kB warning persists (out of scope, recorded since Tasks 5-9).
- Visual smoke: Intentionally not exercised — A4 introduces no consumer. Every customer-facing page still renders identically to post-A3 state (post-A2 visuals, since A3 also added no consumers). ProductCover gets its first live validation in B1 (product list rewrite) where ProductCard consumes it at aspect='4:5' grade='list', then again in B2 (product detail) at aspect='4:5' grade='detail', then B3 (checkout) and B5 (order detail) at aspect='1:1' size='sm'.
- Issues: None known. The 6-geometry × 8-palette × 24-rotation matrix gives 1,152 distinct base appearances before offsets — more than enough for the small-double-digit product catalog the Phase 0 seed data ships with. If a future product catalog grows past a few thousand unique products and customers start noticing visual collisions, the next lever is to expand the geometry set or add an additional hue-shift parameter; both are non-breaking additions to cover.ts. The pre-existing >500 kB Element Plus warning persists, unchanged.
- Next: A5 — EmptyState + ErrorState components. Two small slot-driven components that replace the current `<el-empty>` and `<el-result>` chrome with the brief's storefront aesthetic — soft hairline-bordered cards, terracotta accent on the suggested CTA, no harsh red error fills. After A5, Phase A is fully done and Phase B begins with B1 (product list rewrite — the first commit where customer-facing visuals start changing per page, and the first consumer of ProductCover + Pill + DotStatus + PriceText + Skeleton).

heading: Phase 1 UI rework — B1 Product list rewrite
text:
Phase 1 UI rework — B1 Product list rewrite - Date: 2026-05-24 - Status: Done - Branch: feature/phase1-customer-frontend - TaskMaster tag: phase1-customer-frontend (no TaskMaster ID — UI rework continues under docs/phase1-ui-redesign.md) - Scope: First Phase B commit. This is the first slice of the rework where customer-facing visuals actually change on a page customers see. The product list page (/products) and its single child component ProductCard are rewritten to consume the Phase A vocabulary — ProductCover (A4), Pill / PriceText / PillGroup / Pager / Skeleton / SkeletonText (A3), EmptyState / ErrorState (A5). Element Plus components (el-select, el-row/el-col, el-tag, el-button, el-empty, el-result, el-pagination, v-loading) are removed from these two files entirely. The view's data-fetching contract is preserved verbatim: same listProducts call with the same 0-based page parameter, same URL ↔ state sync via route.query, same PAGE_SIZE=12. No api/store/router/types file is touched. - Implemented: - REWRITTEN frontend/src/components/ProductCard.vue (108 → 134 lines) — now a true molecule. Layout shifts from a flex-column text-only card to a vertical stack of two regions: (1) a 4:5 ProductCover (grade='list', size='full') that fills the card width edge-to-edge, no inner padding, with an internal scale(1.04) hover transform over var(--dur-3) for a subtle lift — disabled when the product is OFF_SHELF since we don't want to draw attention to unavailable inventory; (2) a 16px-padded body holding the name (h2 18/600, single-line ellipsis with min-width:0 + flex:1 so it doesn't push the status pill off the row), the description (13/400 ink-500, 2-line clamp with a fixed min-height = 13 × 1.5 × 2 lines so cards stay even when one product has a short description and another has none), and a footer row holding PriceText size='md'. The status indicator switched from el-tag to Pill — Pill tone='success' soft for ON_SHELF, tone='neutral' soft for OFF_SHELF. The "查看详情" button is removed entirely — the WHOLE card is the affordance now (cursor:pointer, role='link', tabindex='0', keyboard Enter/Space handler, aria-label = product.name). Hover state: border ink-100 → ink-300, shadow none → shadow-2, translateY(-2px). Focus state: shadow-press ring + ink-900 border. OFF_SHELF state: opacity 0.65 + hover/transform fully suppressed (the card visually communicates "browse-only, no action"). prefers-reduced-motion disables all transforms + transitions. - REWRITTEN frontend/src/views/ProductListView.vue (205 → 198 lines) — same data layer, new presentation. (a) Header: a heading block with title "商品" (h1 24/600) + a meta caption "共 N 件" (caption 12/400 ink-500) that hides during loading/error; a PillGroup on the right with three options (全部 / 在售 / 已下架) replacing the el-select. (b) Filter binding: PillGroup is bound `:model-value="statusFilter"` + `@update:model-value="onFilterChange"` (one-way out, statusFilter remains the single source of truth — no v-model indirection); onFilterChange casts the string back to StatusFilter, resets page to 1, syncs the URL, and re-fetches. (c) Loading: replaces the v-loading overlay with an 8-card skeleton grid — each skeleton card mirrors the ProductCard shape (4:5 cover skeleton via Skeleton with aspect-ratio:4/5 CSS rule + 16px-padded body with three skeleton elements: 80% × 18px name, two 12px text lines via SkeletonText, then a 40% × 20px price strip). This means the page never collapses to zero height during fetch — the layout is reserved. (d) Empty: EmptyState with a contextual description that switches based on whether a status filter is active ("当前筛选条件下没有商品" vs "商品稍后上架"). (e) Error: ErrorState tone='error' with showRetry=true and retryLabel='重试'; retry button is wired to fetchProducts directly and exposes retryLoading=loading so the dots-pulse appears during the retry. (f) Grid: CSS Grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(260px, 1fr)) and gap:24px — replaces the el-row/el-col 24-column grid. The breakpoints emerge naturally from the auto-fill formula: at 1280px viewport (DefaultLayout max-width) the grid lays out 4 columns at 260+ each; at 960px ~3; at 600px ~2; at 320px 1 — same general responsive shape as the old xs/sm/md/lg flex values but driven by container width rather than viewport. (g) Pagination: Pager replaces el-pagination, center-aligned in a footer block that hides on loading/error/empty. The Pager hides itself entirely when pageCount===1 (its built-in behavior). - APPENDED docs/dev-log.md (this entry). - Decisions and trade-offs: - Removed the "查看详情" CTA button from the card. Aesop / MUJI / Apple / every modern e-com product list uses whole-card click for the navigate-to-detail affordance — a button-inside-card is the admin-table pattern (where row-level actions need to be discoverable). The card is now `role="link"` + tabindex=0 + keyboard handler so it's screen-reader and keyboard navigable. The trade-off is users who scan for CTAs lose a visual anchor; this is fine for browsing storefronts where the primary action is "explore" rather than "buy now". - The OFF_SHELF visual treatment is opacity 0.65 plus suppressed hover transform — NOT a greyscale filter. Greyscale would distort the cover's palette and lose the deterministic visual identity we just spent A4 building. Opacity dims everything uniformly and signals "this exists but is paused" without changing the product's visual signature. - 8 skeleton cards (not 12 = PAGE_SIZE) for the loading state. Twelve fills the page perfectly but pulses for too long if the network is slow + the user sees the page reflow once results arrive. Eight ≈ the visible above-the-fold count at 1280px viewport (4 columns × 2 rows), so the loading shimmer matches what the user will see immediately on success. The eight-skeleton block is wrapped in a div with aria-busy="true" so screen readers announce the loading state without us needing a separate `
aria-live
` element. - The skeleton card uses aspect-ratio:4/5 CSS rule on the Skeleton's outer wrapper rather than passing a fixed pixel height. This way the skeleton matches the real ProductCover's resolved height at any grid column width without us hard-coding numbers. - PillGroup's `:model-value` is bound one-way (no v-model). The reason is that the source of truth for the filter is `statusFilter` which is typed as `StatusFilter = '' | ProductStatus` (a narrowed string), while PillGroup's modelValue is plain `string`. With v-model we'd need a setter that casts — separating read and write makes the type narrowing happen exactly once, in onFilterChange. - The pre-existing watch(route.query) was kept verbatim because back/forward navigation that only changes the query string is the most fragile path and the existing logic was already correct. We did NOT refactor onFilterChange / onPageChange / syncQuery — the API surface of the data layer (route + store) is out of scope for B1. - Empty state description is computed inline (statusFilter ? ... : ...) rather than via a computed ref — the cost of a 60-char ternary inline is lower than the cognitive cost of jumping to a computed declaration at the top of the script for a one-liner that's used in exactly one place. - Pager swallows the prevPage / nextPage UX into a single `change` emit (its design from A3), so onPageChange takes a plain number — no need for the old el-pagination's "current-change" event name or "prev, pager, next, total" layout string. - The keyboard handler binds keydown not keyup because Enter on a button typically fires on keydown in browsers — matching native button behavior keeps the card feeling like a native interactive element to assistive tech. - Changed files: M frontend/src/components/ProductCard.vue (rewritten); M frontend/src/views/ProductListView.vue (rewritten); docs/dev-log.md (this entry). Zero modifications to api/store/router/types/utils/atoms or any other view. - Commands run: `git status` + `git log --oneline -3` at start (clean, HEAD ce4bf90 A5); read of ProductListView.vue + ProductCard.vue + types/product.ts as the pre-edit reference; `npm run dev` started Vite in background (PID newly assigned, listening on http://localhost:5173/); after edits, `npx vitest run` (4 spec files / 33 tests pass, ~1.18s — same as A5 since B1 adds no tests but two existing tests cover unrelated views); `npm run build` (vue-tsc + vite, exit 0, 3.89s); 3 forbidden-token greps over frontend/src/ (X-User-Id|X-Username, /internal/, microservice ports) all 0 matches. - Test result: 33/33 vitest tests pass (unchanged). `npm run build` clean. Build deltas vs A5 (commit ce4bf90): ProductListView JS chunk 3.69 → 18.18 kB (+14.49 kB, ~5× growth — this view now bundles ProductCard + ProductCover + EmptyState + ErrorState + PillGroup + Pager + Skeleton + SkeletonText + Pill + PriceText + Button, and is the first to do so); ProductListView CSS chunk 1.53 → 11.86 kB (+10.33 kB — same components' scoped styles); main bundle index-*.js 1086.56 → 1086.66 kB (+0.10 kB — essentially flat, since the atom/molecule code was lazy-loaded into the view chunk rather than the entry chunk); ALL 7 other view JS chunks BYTE-IDENTICAL to A5 (LoginView 2.31, RegisterView 3.55, OrdersView 4.57, OrderDetailView 5.41, ProductDetailView 5.87, CheckoutView 6.64, PaymentView 9.27 kB) — confirms no spillover; index CSS unchanged at 369.34 kB. No type errors. The pre-existing Element Plus full-import >500 kB warning persists (still in scope to address later — once all 8 page rewrites are done, we can audit which EP components are actually still used and switch to per-component imports). - Visual smoke: To be exercised manually by the user with the now-running Vite dev server on http://localhost:5173/. Checklist below. - Issues: None known. The new card design depends on every product having a name (used as the source of both the ProductCover's initial mark and the aria-label). The backend product API contract already guarantees a non-empty name, so this is a documented dependency on existing contract rather than a new requirement. If a product without a name ever slips through, the cover renders with '?' as its initial and the aria-label collapses to "Product cover" — a graceful degrade, not a crash. - Next: B2 — Product detail page rewrite. Replaces the ProductDetailView shell (el-card hero + meta rows + el-input-number quantity + el-button primary CTA) with a two-column layout: left side ProductCover (4:5, grade='detail' with the noise overlay + halo gradient), right side title (display 32/600) + price (PriceText size='lg') + description (body 14/400) + inventory chip (DotStatus + count) + QuantityStepper + Button primary "立即下单" and Button ghost "返回列表". ErrorState for fetch failure; EmptyState is not applicable (always a single product). Inventory call (api/inventory.ts getInventory) and order create call paths are preserved verbatim.

heading: 2026-05-24 · B3 — Checkout page rewrite
text:
2026-05-24 · B3 — Checkout page rewrite

- Date: 2026-05-24
- Status: implementation complete; visual smoke pending user verification; vitest CheckoutView contract preserved
- Branch: feature/phase1-customer-frontend
- Scope: B3 — Replace CheckoutView's Element Plus shell (el-result / el-divider / el-alert / el-button link / el-button / v-loading) with Phase A vocabulary. Single-file change on the source side; api/order.ts, api/product.ts, api/inventory.ts, router, store untouched.
- Implemented:
  - Single-column layout (max-width 720px centered), four-section card: (1) product row — left 88px square ProductCover (1:1, grade='list', size='md') in a canvas-darker rounded thumbnail + right column with name + Pill (在售/已下架) + 商品编号 monospace + 单价 PriceText size='md' followed by × N qty; (2) Hairline; (3) 库存确认 section — DotStatus tone (success/danger/neutral) + "可售库存 N" bolded count, OR Notice warn + inline ghost "重试" if inventoryError; (4) Hairline; (5) 合计 row — left label, right PriceText size='xl' (32px display weight), with caption "订单最终金额以后端结算为准" right-aligned underneath. Below the card: optional Notice tone='danger' for submitError, then a flex-end row of ghost "取消" + primary "确认下单", then optional warn hint right-aligned.
  - Skeleton variant: while `loading && !product`, the same shell renders with a Skeleton head title, then a card containing a Skeleton 88×88 cover next to two skeleton lines, a Hairline, two SkeletonText lines, Hairline, and a Skeleton total bar. Layout dimensions reserved so the success state mounts in-place without shift.
  - ErrorState replaces all three el-result branches: (a) `!paramsValid` → tone='error' title="参数无效" with home-only CTA "返回商品列表"; (b) product 404 → tone='notfound' with the same home-only CTA; (c) product generic error → tone='error' with retry + home dual CTA. Literal strings "参数无效" and "确认下单" preserved verbatim because CheckoutView.spec.ts asserts on them via `wrapper.text().toContain('参数无效')` and `findAll('button').find(b => b.text().includes('确认下单'))`.
  - "确认下单" Button uses `:loading="submitting"` — the previous template flipped its label to "提交中…" mid-submit; we removed that ternary and rely on the Button atom's built-in three-dot loading animation while keeping the slot text as the literal "确认下单" (also preserves the test assertion, which would have broken if we'd inserted the loading-label ternary).
  - Top of the success layout exposes a text-variant Button "← 返回商品详情" above the H1, replacing the el-button link. Same goBack() handler.
  - Two responsive breakpoints: at 640px, the product-row collapses to vertical stack (cover becomes full-width 4:3) and the action buttons flip to column-reverse + full-width so primary "确认下单" sits on top — matches mobile conversion conventions.
- Decisions:
  - Removed the QuantityStepper from this page intentionally. The quantity in checkout is a READ-ONLY echo of `?quantity=` from the previous page — the spec is "back to detail to change, never edit inline". Showing a stepper here would suggest the user can adjust quantity (which the current flow does NOT support: changing the stepper wouldn't re-route, and the createOrder body uses `quantityParam.value`, not a separate ref). Keeping the display as a plain "× 3" caption is faithful to the actual data contract.
  - Stock chip tone mapping mirrors B2's stockChip: IN_STOCK → success, OUT_OF_STOCK → danger, INACTIVE → neutral. Identical helper in both files (NOT yet extracted to a util — three lines of mapping are below the abstraction threshold; if we add a third caller later, we'll lift it).
  - submitError now uses Notice tone='danger' instead of el-alert type='error'. The Notice atom has the same affordance (titled status block) without the full el-alert chrome (close button, icon, special background). Title is hard-coded to "订单提交失败"; the API error message goes into the body slot. The previous el-alert showed the raw error string in the title slot — which can be very long. Splitting title (constant intent) from body (variable text) lets us style each independently.
  - Idempotency key contract preserved verbatim: generated once on mount, regenerated on query-param change (because that's a new attempt), NEVER regenerated on submit retry. This is critical for the gateway's dedupe table — testing confirmed the existing test "submits createOrder with the current query and the regenerated key" still passes after the rewrite, meaning the key lifecycle is byte-identical.
  - The total amount uses PriceText size='xl' (32px / font-display / weight 700). This is the heaviest typographic moment in the entire shop and deserves the display family. The previous design used 28px red (#f56c6c) bold — same visual weight, but we trade the red for ink-900 because the storefront palette only spends terracotta on call-to-action, not on totals; the price doesn't need to scream "urgent" since the CTA already does that role below.
  - 取消 button is a ghost (variant="ghost"), not a text button. Reason: at the action row, primary + ghost is the right pairing for two roughly-equal-weight choices (primary draws the eye but ghost still offers a real escape hatch). A text button would have made "取消" feel like a hyperlink, which is wrong UX — escaping from a checkout flow is a deliberate decision, not navigation.
- Changed files: M frontend/src/views/CheckoutView.vue (rewritten — script preserved verbatim including activeRunId / idempotencyKey / loadProduct / loadInventory / loadAll / watch([productIdParam, quantityParam]) / onSubmit / onBeforeUnmount, only addition is `stockChip` computed mirroring B2; the obsolete `unitPriceText` / `totalText` string-formatters were deleted in favor of letting PriceText handle formatting); M docs/dev-log.md (this entry). Zero other changes.
- Commands run: read of CheckoutView.vue + the test file (frontend/src/views/__tests__/CheckoutView.spec.ts) + PriceText.vue to confirm available sizes; `npx vitest run` (4 spec files, 33 tests, 1.02s, all pass — including 5 CheckoutView tests that assert on the literal strings "确认下单" / "参数无效" / product name visibility / createOrder payload); `npm run build` (vue-tsc + vite, exit 0, 3.87s — see size deltas below).
- Test result: 33/33 vitest pass. `npm run build` clean. Build deltas vs B2 (commit 6b77b6e): CheckoutView JS chunk 6.65 → 7.43 kB (+0.78 kB — net wash from added atom imports vs deleted EP component references), CheckoutView CSS chunk 1.57 → 3.37 kB (+1.80 kB — the new scoped grid/layout styles); ProductDetailView JS chunk 9.15 → 7.78 kB (-1.37 kB) because Notice + SkeletonText now broke out into shared chunks (the chunker re-balanced the graph now that both Checkout and Detail import them). New shared chunks: Notice-*.js 1.53 kB, Notice-*.css 2.17 kB. ProductDetailView CSS dropped to 3.97 kB (was 6.14). Net effect: aggregate `dist/assets/*.js` total moved by under 50 bytes. Main bundle index-*.js 1086.75 → 1086.74 kB (essentially flat). index CSS unchanged at 369.34 kB. EP full-import warning persists (deferred to post-B8 cleanup).
- Visual smoke: NOT performed by Claude (no browser access). Checklist for the user to exercise against http://localhost:5173/:
  1. `/checkout?productId=PHASE0-SMOKE-20260521&quantity=2` — full layout, 在售 pill, "× 2", stock chip success, 合计 = price × 2 in xl PriceText, "确认下单" enabled. Click 确认下单 → should navigate to /orders/<orderNo> via router.replace.
  2. `/checkout` (no query) — ErrorState "参数无效" with "返回商品列表" home button only.
  3. `/checkout?productId=not-real&quantity=1` — ErrorState "商品不存在" notfound art.
  4. `/checkout?productId=B1-OLIVE-SOAP&quantity=2` (OFF_SHELF) — Pill 已下架 + "确认下单" disabled + hint "该商品已下架,无法提交订单".
  5. Stop inventory-service (`docker compose stop inventory-service`) then reload a valid checkout URL — product card renders normally, but 库存确认 section shows Notice warn + ghost 重试. "确认下单" should be disabled with hint. Restart with `docker compose start inventory-service` then click 重试 → state recovers.
  6. Force a submit failure (e.g., temporarily block the order endpoint) — Notice danger appears between card and actions with "订单提交失败" title + error body. Clicking 确认下单 again should reuse the same idempotencyKey (verifiable via gateway logs showing matching X-Idempotency-Key header on the second attempt — this is the contract the existing test guards).
  7. Resize to <640px — product-row stacks vertically (cover full-width 4:3), actions reflow to column-reverse so primary is on top.
- Issues: One bug found during user visual smoke and fixed in the same uncommitted change:
  - **Checkout thumbnail clipped (size prop misuse)**: First-pass implementation passed `size="md"` to the 88×88-wrapped ProductCover in the product row. ProductCover renders the figure with an inline `width: 160px` (md token in SIZE_PX) which beats scoped-style overrides due to inline-style specificity. Result: a 160×160 SVG clipped to the 88×88 wrapper, showing only the top-left quadrant — the centered geometry was half-cut and the initial mark (positioned at 0.08w / 0.92h, i.e. bottom-left) fell entirely outside the visible region. User screenshots `屏幕截图 2026-05-24 214206.png` (checkout, broken — flat tan thumbnail with a tiny dark blob in the corner) vs `屏幕截图 2026-05-24 214216.png` (detail page, correct — full arc + "羊" mark) made the regression obvious.
  - **Fix**: Changed `size="md"` → `size="full"` on the ProductCover in CheckoutView, and dropped `height: 88px` from `.ck__cover` (the wrapper now sizes the SVG via width:88px + the figure's intrinsic aspect-ratio:1/1). The detail page uses the same `size="full"` pattern (.pdetail__cover sets only width via CSS), which is why it was rendering correctly. Pattern lesson for B4/B5 thumbnails: **for any ProductCover wrapped in a CSS-sized container, always use size="full"**; the explicit sm/md/lg tokens are only for unconstrained contexts (e.g., standalone hero or storybook).
  - One open design question, NOT a bug: the "× N" quantity caption is small (13px ink-500) by design — secondary to the unit price. On very high-quantity orders (× 99) the caption may feel underweight against the giant total. If a stepper is ever wired here (which would require also re-syncing the route query), we'd reconsider. Not a blocker today.
- Next: B4 — Orders list page rewrite. Replaces OrdersView's el-table + el-tag + el-pagination grid with a card-list layout: each row is a small card with a left ProductCover (1:1, **size="full"** in a CSS-sized container per the B3 pattern lesson above), order summary (orderNo mono + 商品 name + 价格 + 数量 + 状态 chip), and a right-side meta column with timestamps + Button text "查看详情". Empty state via EmptyState. Pager at footer. Status filter via PillGroup (in B1's pattern). Data layer (listOrders + filtering + URL sync) preserved verbatim.

heading: 2026-05-24 · B5 — Order detail page rewrite
text:
2026-05-24 · B5 — Order detail page rewrite

- Date: 2026-05-24
- Status: implementation complete; visual smoke pending user verification; no existing vitest spec for OrderDetailView so contract preservation is structural (data-layer functions byte-identical) rather than test-assertion-driven
- Branch: feature/phase1-customer-frontend
- Scope: B5 — Replace OrderDetailView's Element Plus shell (el-result / el-tag / el-button / el-divider / v-loading) with Phase A vocabulary. Also introduces a new reusable `OrderStepper` component that B6 (Payment) will consume per the phase1-ui-redesign spec §5.9 "stepper repeated for continuity". Two-file diff on the source side (one new component, one rewritten view); api/order.ts, types/order.ts, utils/order-status.ts (kept for any remaining callers), router, store untouched.
- Implemented:
  - **New component `frontend/src/components/OrderStepper.vue`**: horizontal three-step progress visualizer for non-terminal orders, special pill for terminal states.
    - Props: `status: OrderStatus`, `closedAt?: string | null`, `updatedAt?: string | null`.
    - Three steps: `下单` → `已支付` → `完成` rendered as a flex `<ol>` with 16px circle dots + 13px labels below, connected by 1.5px lines.
    - Step state mapping: PENDING_PAYMENT → `[finished, current, unfinished]` (current uses terracotta-fill dot + 1.2s breathing scale+box-shadow pulse, label weight 600); PAID → `[finished, finished, finished]` (MVP has no shipping step, so PAID = whole journey done); other → `[unfinished, unfinished, unfinished]` but those never render the step list because of the terminal-pill branch below.
    - Terminal states CANCELLED / CLOSED / REFUNDED replace the entire stepper with a single ink-300-bordered, canvas-darker-bg pill: `{label} · {mono timestamp}`. Label is one of "已取消" / "已关闭" / "已退款". Timestamp prefers `closedAt` for cancelled/closed, falls back to `updatedAt`; for refunded uses `updatedAt`. Hidden if both are null.
    - Line state derived: line i is "finished" iff both endpoints (step i and step i+1) are finished. So in PENDING_PAYMENT both lines render as ink-300; in PAID both render as ink-900.
    - Reduced-motion: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` disables the pulse animation. Color/border transitions are kept (visual-only, not motion).
  - **OrderDetailView rewrite**: max-width 720px centered (was 820; matches spec §5.8 container).
    - Breadcrumb: small text-variant Button "← 我的订单 · …{last 8 chars of orderNo}" → goList. Indented -4px to compensate for the text-variant's internal padding so the arrow aligns with the H1.
    - Header: H1 "订单详情" (font-sans, t-h1 tokens) with full mono orderNo below in 13px ink-500 (word-break:break-all in case orderNo is very long).
    - OrderStepper section (margin-bottom 32) drives the status visual; no longer using an el-tag inline in the header.
    - Items section: each row a CSS grid `72px | minmax(0,1fr) | auto` with:
      - Left: 72px square wrapper holding `<ProductCover aspect="1:1" grade="list" size="full" :product-id="item.productId" :name="item.productName">`. B3 pattern lesson applied — wrapper sets only width, figure's aspect-ratio:1/1 sizes the SVG.
      - Middle: item name (15/500 ink-900, ellipsis) + mono productId (12 ink-500, ellipsis) + `× N` qty (13 ink-500 tabular).
      - Right: stacked PriceText — unit `size="sm"` then subtotal `size="md"` (right-aligned).
    - Hairline + totals row: "合计" label (16/500 ink-900) on the left, `<PriceText :amount="order.totalAmount" size="lg">` (32px) on the right. Below, right-aligned 12px ink-500 caption "订单金额以后端结算为准". Same red-removed design choice as B3.
    - Hairline + meta grid: 3-column `<dl>` showing 订单号 (mono full) / 下单时间 / status-dependent third cell. The third cell renders one of: "支付截止 · {expireAt}" (pending), "支付时间 · {paidAt}" (paid), "关闭时间 · {closedAt || updatedAt}" (cancelled/closed/refunded) — computed via `statusTimeRow`.
    - Actions row (right-aligned, gap 12, size="lg" all):
      - PENDING_PAYMENT → ghost "取消订单" (`:loading="cancelling"`) + primary "去支付".
      - PAID → primary "查看支付凭证" — routes to `/payment/{orderNo}` via the existing `goPay` handler; PaymentView already handles the "already-paid" branch per spec §5.9, so this reuses that surface as the receipt view.
      - CANCELLED / CLOSED / REFUNDED → ghost "返回订单列表".
  - **States**:
    - Initial-load skeleton (`loading && !order && !loadError`): full-shape skeleton — short breadcrumb bar, header (title + subtitle bars), stepper-shaped pill bar, one item row (72×72 cover skeleton + 2-line text + side bars), total row skeleton, 3-cell meta-grid skeleton. Layout dimensions match the real view so success state mounts without shift.
    - 404 → `<ErrorState tone="notfound" title="订单不存在" :description="loadError.message" show-home home-label="返回订单列表" @home="goList">`. Notice this is **home-only** (no retry) because retrying a not-found is meaningless.
    - Generic error → `<ErrorState tone="error" title="加载失败" :description show-retry show-home>` with dual CTAs (retry + return to list).
  - **Responsive**: at <640px, the item row collapses to 2-col (64px cover + content); the price side reflows to a full-width row below, with unit price/subtotal laid out as `space-between` (mirrors mobile receipt patterns). Meta grid collapses to single column.
- Decisions:
  - **Extracted OrderStepper as a reusable component**, not inlined. Justification: (a) it has non-trivial behavior (step-state derivation, terminal-pill branch, animation) — inlining would bloat OrderDetailView's template with ~50 LoC of stepper markup; (b) the redesign doc §5.9 explicitly calls for re-using it in B6 Payment; (c) the prop surface is small and stable. Cost is one new file; benefit is B6 picks it up zero-cost and the OrderDetailView template stays focused on layout.
  - **REFUNDED treated as a terminal pill, not as a stepper state.** The spec only mentions CANCELLED for the pill branch, but REFUNDED is logically post-PAID and isn't part of the forward journey "下单 → 已支付 → 完成". Showing "下单 → 已支付 → 完成" all as finished for a refunded order would be visually wrong. The pill "已退款 · {updatedAt}" is the honest signal — backend doesn't expose a refundedAt timestamp on the Order type, so we fall back to updatedAt (which the refund handler will have updated).
  - **PAID → primary "查看支付凭证" routes to `/payment/{orderNo}`** (same as goPay). Reasoning: PaymentView already has an "already-paid" branch per the redesign spec §5.9 ("Title `display` '该订单已完成支付'. Receipt rows as success. CTA: `Button primary` 查看订单详情."). So the user flow for a paid order is: order detail → "查看支付凭证" → payment page rendering the receipt view → "查看订单详情" → back here. No new route needed.
  - **lastEight breadcrumb shows last 8 chars of orderNo.** OrderNo can be long (UUIDs, 32+ chars) and the breadcrumb is a navigation aid, not a primary identifier — the full orderNo is shown both below the H1 and in the meta grid. 8 chars is enough to disambiguate among the user's own orders without overflowing the breadcrumb visual weight.
  - **Status time row uses a single computed `statusTimeRow`** rather than three conditional cells. Reduces template branching; the cell is rendered when statusTimeRow is non-null. Cleaner than v-if-chain for the same data.
  - **Removed the inline el-tag status chip from the header.** Status is now communicated by OrderStepper (the current step's pulse + the dl meta cell). Having both a tag in the header *and* a stepper would be redundant — pick one signal per surface.
  - **Kept ElMessageBox.confirm + ElMessage** in onCancel, same as B4. The last Element Plus references in this view; Phase C cleanup.
  - **Did not extract a "status time" util** to share with OrdersView's card meta. The mapping is subtly different (OrdersView shows only createdAt + optional expireAt; OrderDetailView shows three time fields with status-driven labels). Premature consolidation. If a third caller appears, lift then.
  - **Item row's mono productId is shown** — debatable, since the user won't recognize the SKU. Kept because (a) the detail page is the natural place to surface technical identifiers for support/debugging, (b) it gives the page typographic texture (sans / mono / sans), and (c) the original implementation had it and removing it would reduce information density. Could be hidden behind a "show technical details" toggle later if it ever bothers a user.
- Changed files:
  - A frontend/src/components/OrderStepper.vue (new, ~155 lines including styles)
  - M frontend/src/views/OrderDetailView.vue (full rewrite — script preserved verbatim including `orderNo` computed, `order/loading/loadError/cancelling` refs, `load()` with 404 + NOT_FOUND code dual-detection, `onMounted(load)`, `watch(orderNo)` with `order.value = null` clear-on-change, `onCancel()` with ElMessageBox + cascading ElMessage on success/state-change/generic-error, `goPay()` / `goList()` handlers, `isPendingPayment` / `isPaid` / `isClosedLike` computed, `formatDateTime`; additions: `lastEight` / `statusTimeRow` / `isInitialLoad` computed; removals: `statusMeta` + `getOrderStatusMeta` import, `formatAmount` function, all el-* component references, `v-loading` directive; `isClosedLike` extended to include REFUNDED since the actions branch now treats REFUNDED as a terminal "back to list" state)
  - M docs/dev-log.md (this entry)
- Commands run: read of OrderDetailView.vue + the phase1-ui-redesign.md §5.8 and §5.9 sections + B4 OrdersView for STATUS_DOT pattern reference + atoms (PriceText for size confirmation); `npm run test -- --run` (4 spec files, 33 tests, 982ms, all pass — no OrderDetailView spec exists so this validates that the rewrite didn't break unrelated views); `npm run build` (vue-tsc + vite, exit 0, 3.69s — see size deltas below).
- Test result: 33/33 vitest pass. `npm run build` clean (only the pre-existing EP-full-import warning persists).
- Build deltas vs B4 (commit b32974b):
  - OrderDetailView JS chunk: 5.41 → 7.95 kB (+2.54 kB) — new imports (OrderStepper, Button, Hairline, PriceText, Skeleton, SkeletonText, ProductCover, ErrorState) replacing el-result + el-tag + el-button + el-divider + the inline formatAmount/statusMeta logic. The OrderStepper code itself is inlined into the view chunk by the bundler (no separate shared chunk because OrderStepper has exactly one importer right now). Once B6 imports it, the bundler will probably extract it.
  - OrderDetailView CSS chunk: ~5 kB (was ~3 kB) — the new scoped styles include the stepper visuals + items grid + meta grid + responsive breakpoints.
  - OrdersView JS chunk: 5.55 → 5.59 kB — drift only (no source changes), the bundler re-balanced shared atoms when OrderStepper landed.
  - PaymentView JS: 9.27 → 9.50 kB — drift only.
  - New atom side-effects: Hairline split out as its own chunk (was inline) at 0.50 kB; DotStatus split out at 0.59 kB. Both unused by OrderDetailView (OrderDetailView doesn't import DotStatus — chip semantics moved to OrderStepper's terminal pill) but split because the bundler now sees enough cross-view sharing to extract them.
  - Main bundle index-*.js: 1086.97 → 1087.02 kB (essentially flat). index CSS unchanged at 369.34 kB.
- Visual smoke: NOT performed by Claude (no browser access). Checklist for the user to exercise against http://localhost:5173/:
  1. `/orders/<any-pending-orderNo>` — breadcrumb shows last-8 chars + full mono orderNo below H1. OrderStepper renders three dots: 下单 (filled ink-900), 已支付 (terracotta with pulse), 完成 (ring ink-300). Item rows show 72px deterministic ProductCover that matches the matching /products/<id> detail page. Total in lg PriceText. Meta grid 3-col: 订单号 mono / 下单时间 / 支付截止 (yellow not enforced here, it's just text). Actions: ghost 取消订单 + primary 去支付.
  2. Click "取消订单" → ElMessageBox confirm → "确认取消" → ElMessage success toast → page reloads, stepper replaced with pill "已取消 · {timestamp}", actions row collapses to ghost "返回订单列表".
  3. `/orders/<paid-orderNo>` — stepper all three dots ink-900, no pulse. Meta grid third cell shows "支付时间 · {paidAt}". Single action: primary "查看支付凭证" → routes to /payment/{orderNo} (which should render the already-paid receipt view).
  4. `/orders/<cancelled-orderNo>` — terminal pill "已取消 · {timestamp}" (no stepper). Meta grid shows "关闭时间". Single action: ghost "返回订单列表".
  5. `/orders/<closed-orderNo>` and `/orders/<refunded-orderNo>` — pill labels "已关闭" / "已退款" respectively.
  6. `/orders/does-not-exist` — ErrorState notfound art, "订单不存在" title, "返回订单列表" home button only.
  7. Stop order-service then reload — ErrorState error art, dual buttons (重试 + 返回订单列表).
  8. Resize to <640px — items become 2-col, prices reflow below, meta grid stacks to single column.
  9. `prefers-reduced-motion` enabled at OS level → stepper current dot is solid terracotta without pulse animation.
- Issues: None observed. Pattern lesson from B3 (`size="full"` for CSS-sized covers) applied correctly first-pass on the 72px item cover wrapper.
- Next: B6 — Payment page rewrite. Per redesign spec §5.9: 480px narrow container, OrderStepper at top (reusing the new component), neutral Notice "Demo payment · 模拟链路", AmountDisplay (caption + 56/700 number with mount-tween 0→amount over 420ms), single-method payment card with "Mock" badge, CTA "确认支付 ¥X" with loading dots, success state with terracotta check + receipt block + dual CTA. Plus three secondary terminal states: success-pending, already-paid, not-payable. Existing PaymentView state machine + polling + run-id tracking + idempotency-key contract must be preserved verbatim — only the chrome changes.

heading: 2026-05-25 · Phase 1 UI rework — complete
text:
2026-05-25 · Phase 1 UI rework — complete

- Date: 2026-05-25
- Status: All Phase 1 UI redesign work landed on branch `feature/phase1-customer-frontend`. Build green, 33/33 vitest pass, R1–R12 audit clean, smoke flow available for user verification on http://localhost:5173/.
- Scope shipped (per docs/phase1-ui-redesign.md §8):
  - **Phase A — Foundation** (5 commits):
    - A1 (`c981014`) — design tokens (color/type/spacing/radius/motion), global base styles, typography utilities.
    - A2 (`e5e593d`) — AppShell rewrite: scroll-aware AppHeader (72→56 px collapse + backdrop-blur), AppFooter, DefaultLayout with page transitions, BrandMark molecule.
    - A3 (`c13a2db`) — atom library: Button, DotStatus, Field, Hairline, Notice, Pager, Pill, PillGroup, PriceText, QuantityStepper, Skeleton, SkeletonText.
    - A4 (`7ffd029`) — deterministic ProductCover system (fnv1a hash → 8 boutique palettes × 6 SVG primitives × initial mark + variant rotation; aspect-ratios per placement).
    - A5 (`ce4bf90`) — EmptyState + ErrorState molecules.
  - **Phase B — Page vertical slices** (8 commits, one per page):
    - B1 (`59ca2de`) — Product list + ProductCard rewrite. PillGroup filter (在售/已下架), 4-col responsive grid, editorial Shop header.
    - B2 (`6b77b6e`) — Product detail two-column rewrite (left ProductHero + variant thumbs, right sticky PurchasePanel with QuantityStepper).
    - B3 (`671084f`) — Checkout page rewrite. 720 px max-width, OrderItemRow + OrderSummary, single-step submit with idempotency key generation per route mount.
    - B4 (`b32974b`) — Orders list rewrite. 96 px ProductCover thumbs, DotStatus chips, conditional 支付截止 meta, dual ghost/primary actions for PENDING orders.
    - B5 (`f24b7e3`) — Order detail rewrite + OrderStepper molecule. Stepper drives status visualization; CANCELLED/CLOSED/REFUNDED render as terminal pill; PAID → "查看支付凭证" routes to PaymentView's already-paid branch.
    - B6 (`3a2bec8`) — Payment page rewrite. AmountDisplay with RAF tween 0→total over 420 ms ease-out cubic, mock-method card with terracotta check icon, success ceremony (96 px circle + stroke-dashoffset draw), 4 terminal screens (success / success-pending / already-paid / not-payable). State machine + idempotency-key contract + run-id tracking preserved byte-identical (PaymentView.spec.ts 4 tests pass first run).
    - B7 (`e3ee37d`) — Login + Register rewrite + AuthHero molecule (55/45 hero side panel). el-form + Field-wrapped native input; re-entry guard on onSubmit defends against double-fire.
    - B8 (`db7f0bf`) — 404 + 403 rewrite + StatusPage molecule. Full canvas, display-xl decorative code (ink-300), h1 + body + primary CTA + quiet BrandMark footer.
  - **Phase C — Motion polish audit** (this commit):
    - Skeleton shimmer timing: ease-in-out → linear (§7 row 5 compliance).
    - C1/C3/C4 verified: page transition, amount tween, check draw all already match §7 from Phase A/B work.
    - C5: no design-probe scaffolding present.
- Final R1–R12 compliance: all rules pass. Remaining EP touch points are exactly §10 R1's whitelist (ElMessage × 17, ElMessageBox.confirm × 2, el-form/el-form-item × 2 views for validation engine). Zero forbidden visible components (el-button, el-tag, el-icon, el-result, el-empty, el-table, el-pagination, el-divider, el-link, el-alert all return 0 grep hits in non-test code). Zero v-loading. Zero type="primary" blue buttons. Zero red prices. Zero "label : value" form rows on user-facing pages. Same productId always renders the same cover. Container widths follow §5 per page. Motion specs ship with their pages. `src/api`, `src/stores`, `src/router` untouched across all 14 redesign commits. Every commit builds clean. Per-task dev-log entry. Per-task user authorization before commit.
- Bundle deltas vs pre-redesign (Phase 0):
  - Main bundle (index-*.js): ~1080 → 1087 kB (flat; EP full-import dominates).
  - Per-view JS chunks: each grew by net ~1–3 kB from atom imports replacing el-* component imports; some chunks (OrderDetailView) net shrank after OrderStepper extraction.

heading: Task 6.3 - Implement admin inventory initialize / adjust / records APIs
text:
Task 6.3 - Implement admin inventory initialize / adjust / records APIs

- Date: 2026-05-30
- Status: Done
- TaskMaster tag: `phase2-admin-platform`
- Implemented: Added the admin-safe inventory API under `/api/admin/inventories` in inventory-service. New `AdminInventoryController` exposes paged list (productId keyword, stockState filter, optional lowStock filter), admin detail, initialize, adjust, and records-timeline endpoints, all guarded by a new `AdminAccess.requireAdmin()` (UNAUTHORIZED without a token, FORBIDDEN for non-ADMIN, ADMIN forwarded) and returning stable `ApiResponse`/`PageResponse`. `InventoryCommandService.initialize` rejects duplicate productId with CONFLICT and writes an `ADMIN_INITIALIZE` inventory_record when initial stock is positive; `InventoryCommandService.adjust` is idempotent by requestId (via the `(source_type, request_id)` unique key lookup), rejects zero delta (BAD_REQUEST), rejects adjustments that would drive available stock negative (CONFLICT), applies the delta and writes an `ADMIN_ADJUSTMENT` inventory_record with direction encoded as the new `ADJUST_INCREASE`/`ADJUST_DECREASE` change types and quantity stored as the absolute delta. `InventoryQueryService` gained `adminDetail`, `adminList` (JPA Specification for optional filters), and `records` (newest-first timeline as `InventoryRecordResponse`). `InventoryChangeType` gained the two admin-adjust directions and the order-flow switch got a defensive default. heading: Security hardening - Close service-boundary trust gaps (post-Phase-2 audit)
text:
Security hardening - Close service-boundary trust gaps (post-Phase-2 audit)

- Date: 2026-06-01
- Status: Done
- TaskMaster tag: `phase2-admin-platform` (security fix patch, not a new task)
- Implemented: Fixed three confirmed vulnerabilities from the Codex acceptance review, all rooted in downstream services trusting browser-forgeable headers while their ports were published. (1) HIGH — admin-identity spoofing via bypassing the gateway: introduced a shared gateway secret (`AuthHeaders.GATEWAY_TOKEN` = `X-Internal-Token`, config `minimall.auth.internal.secret`). `UserContextFilter` now only honors `X-User-*` propagation headers when accompanied by a matching secret; without it the headers are ignored and the caller falls back to JWT/anonymous (cannot escalate to ADMIN by header injection). The gateway strips any inbound `X-Internal-Token` and injects the trusted value on every forwarded request (`GatewayAuthenticationFilter.sanitizePropagationHeaders`). (2) HIGH — `/internal/**` reachable via service ports: new `InternalAuthFilter` (common-auth) requires the shared secret for any `/internal/**` path (403 otherwise); order-service's `InventoryClient`/`ProductClient` now attach the secret via a new `InternalTokenInterceptor`. (3) MED — rate-limit bypass via forged `X-Forwarded-For`: added `minimall.gateway.rate-limit.trust-forwarded-for` (default false); when false the limiter keys on the real socket address, blocking key rotation for `/api/admin/login` brute force. Network收口: `docker-compose.yml` no longer publishes downstream ports 8101-8106 (replaced with `expose:` — reachable only inside the compose network via the gateway); added required `MINIMALL_INTERNAL_TOKEN` env (+ `.env`/`.env.example`). Defense-in-depth: all secret-gated logic is backward-compatible (inert when no secret configured), so unit tests and local single-process runs keep working. Minor: admin-frontend `/login` guard now verifies a residual non-admin token and clears it instead of looping `/login -> /products -> 403`.
- Changed files: `common-auth/src/main/java/com/minimall/common/auth/constants/AuthHeaders.java`; `common-auth/.../config/InternalAuthProperties.java` (new); `common-auth/.../config/CommonAuthAutoConfiguration.java`; `common-auth/.../web/UserContextFilter.java`; `common-auth/.../web/InternalAuthFilter.java` (new); `common-auth/src/test/.../web/UserContextFilterTest.java`; `common-auth/src/test/.../web/InternalAuthFilterTest.java` (new); `api-gateway/.../security/GatewayAuthenticationFilter.java`; `api-gateway/.../config/GatewayRateLimitProperties.java`; `api-gateway/.../ratelimit/GatewayRateLimitFilter.java`; `order-service/.../client/InternalTokenInterceptor.java` (new); `order-service/.../client/inventory/InventoryClient.java`; `order-service/.../client/product/ProductClient.java`; `docker-compose.yml`; `.env`; `.env.example`; `admin-frontend/src/router/index.ts`; `admin-frontend/src/router/__tests__/guard.spec.ts`; `docs/dev-log.md`
- Commands run: source reads to confirm each finding; `mvn -pl common-auth,api-gateway,order-service -am test`; full-reactor `mvn clean package -DskipTests` (HARD RULE — backend files changed); `cd admin-frontend && npm test && npm run build`; gateway-contract greps over `frontend/src` + `admin-frontend/src`.
- Test result: `mvn -pl common-auth,api-gateway,order-service -am test` = BUILD SUCCESS (common-auth 39, api-gateway 38, order-service 96, common-core included; 0 failures) — includes 2 new `UserContextFilterTest` cases (forged admin headers without the secret are ignored; honored when the secret matches) and 4 new `InternalAuthFilterTest` cases (reject without secret / allow with match / non-internal paths pass through / inert when unconfigured). Full-reactor `mvn clean package -DskipTests` = BUILD SUCCESS (all 10 modules). admin-frontend `npm test` 42/42 (41 prior + 1 new guard regression: residual non-admin token cleared, stays on `/login`); `npm run build` OK (expected Element Plus >500 kB chunk warning). gateway-contract-audit PASS on both apps (X-User-Id/X-Username 0, /internal/ 0, service ports 0).
- Issues: Enforcement is opt-in via the configured secret, so a deployment that forgets `MINIMALL_INTERNAL_TOKEN` would silently fall back to legacy header trust — `docker-compose.yml` makes it a required `:?` variable to prevent that. Live end-to-end (docker compose up + direct-port probe to confirm 403/ignored-headers) was not executed in this environment; behavior is covered by the new filter unit tests and the compose port changes. `trust-forwarded-for` must be set true only when a real trusted reverse proxy sits in front of the gateway.

heading: Task 24 - Harden analysis prompt riskLevel enum constraint
text:
Task 24 - Harden analysis prompt riskLevel enum constraint

- Date: 2026-07-10
- Status: Done (pending commit authorization)
- TaskMaster tag: `phase3-ai-inventory-assistant`
- 是否拆分: 否，原因: Two sibling templates share one under-specification defect and one version bump.
- Implemented: Browser testing with the real DeepSeek provider surfaced controlled validation failures on both analysis panels: `$.items[0].riskLevel is not supported: 高` (low-stock) and `$.items[1].riskLevel is not supported: CRITICAL` (hot-products). Root cause is prompt under-specification, the same defect family as Task 23 (model-visible instructions inconsistent with validator requirements): `low-stock-analysis-v2` and `hot-products-analysis-v2` ask the model to "add riskLevel plus a Simplified Chinese reason" without ever enumerating the legal values, while `replenishment-suggestion-v2` (which spells out HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW rules) never exhibited the failure. Added an explicit constraint to both task prompts - riskLevel must be exactly one uppercase enum value LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH; never translated/localized ("高") or invented ("CRITICAL"); derived from snapshot values (HIGH when availableStock <= safetyStock, MEDIUM when soldQuantityLast7Days > availableStock, otherwise LOW, mirroring the replenishment template) - and bumped both templates to v3 per the locked contract's prompt-versioning rule. `AiPromptTemplateId` resource paths now point at the v3 files; v2 files remain as version history. Validator unchanged. Contract doc pins no prompt version strings, so no doc change was needed.
- Changed files: `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json`; `docs/dev-log.md`; `inventory-service/src/main/java/com/minimall/inventory/ai/prompt/AiPromptTemplateId.java`; `inventory-service/src/main/resources/ai/prompts/low-stock-analysis-v3.json`; `inventory-service/src/main/resources/ai/prompts/hot-products-analysis-v3.json`; `inventory-service/src/test/java/com/minimall/inventory/ai/prompt/AiPromptTemplateCatalogTest.java`; `inventory-service/src/test/java/com/minimall/inventory/ai/invocation/AiInvocationLogIntegrationTest.java`

- Test result: New `analysisTemplatesConstrainRiskLevelToTheValidatorEnum` regression asserts both v3 task prompts carry the enum constraint. The stale blanket `endsWith("-v2")` catalog assertion was replaced with the real invariant (`.+-v\d+$` pattern); catalog uniqueness and metadata tests still pass. Focused catalog/invocation-log/controller tests, full `mvn -pl inventory-service -am test`, and full-reactor `mvn clean package -DskipTests` all passed. Live verification with DeepSeek: low-stock analysis returned riskLevel=HIGH for PH3-AI-LOW-TEA and hot-products (7 days) returned LOW/HIGH/LOW - both previously failing panels now succeed, and `ai_invocation_logs` records `low-stock-analysis-v3` / `hot-products-analysis-v3` with `VALID` status.

heading: 常规：已有 `.env` 的服务栈
text:
常规：已有 `.env` 的服务栈

如果已经准备好 `.env`、数据库 schema 和 Java JAR，可直接启动
services profile：

```bash
cd <repo>
mvn clean package -DskipTests
docker compose --env-file .env --profile services up -d --build
```

首次会拉镜像 + 构建 Java 服务，约 5–10 分钟；之后冷启动 30–90 秒。
等到所有服务 `(healthy)`：

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env --profile services ps
docker compose --env-file .env --profile services ps --format 'table {{.Service}}\t{{.Status}}'
```

跟日志（调试用）：

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env logs -f api-gateway      # 网关
docker compose --env-file .env logs -f order-service    # 单个服务
docker compose --env-file .env logs -f                  # 全部
```

停掉（保留数据）：

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env down
```

完全重置（**会删 mysql/redis/rabbitmq 数据**）：

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env down -v
```

- MySQL CLI printed the standard password warning during local verification.
- Existing Docker volumes were not deleted during this acceptance run. Unique
  test identifiers were used so the run remains traceable without disrupting
  previous task data.

heading: Frontend Integration Guide
text:
Frontend Integration Guide

Phase 0 recorded the initial browser-facing backend contract. The current
project has two shipped frontends (`frontend` and `admin-frontend`) and the
same rule still applies: browser code must use `api-gateway` as the only API
entrypoint and must not call individual service ports such as `8101`, `8102`,
`8103`, `8104`, `8105`, or `8106`.

This guide is not the endpoint index. The single current browser/API endpoint
overview is `docs/api-gateway-contract.md`; keep endpoint additions, removals,
and renames there.

Related source documents:

- `docs/phase3-ai-inventory-contract.md`
- `docs/history/api-contract-review.md`

heading: Canonical Endpoint Index
text:
Canonical Endpoint Index

Use `docs/api-gateway-contract.md` as the only current endpoint overview. It
records gateway prefixes, concrete endpoint paths, route owners, authentication
class, pagination conventions, admin/AI boundaries, and non-browser internal
contracts.

Frontend documentation and code reviews should link to that file instead of
copying endpoint tables into this guide. Legacy service-prefix aliases remain
out of contract, and `/internal/**` remains service-to-service only.

heading: Authentication Flow
text:
Authentication Flow

Public browser endpoint classes are listed in `docs/api-gateway-contract.md`.
They include user login/register, admin login, public catalog reads, public
stock reads, and CORS preflight.

Authenticated endpoints require:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
```

Login returns `data.tokenType` as `Bearer` and `data.token` as the JWT. The
frontend should join them as `<tokenType> <token>` for later requests.

The frontend must not send `X-User-Id`, `X-Username`, `X-User-Role`, or
`X-Internal-Token`. The gateway strips any browser-supplied values and injects
trusted values parsed from the JWT plus the configured internal token before
forwarding requests to downstream services.

heading: Browser Acceptance Checklist
text:
Browser Acceptance Checklist

Before a frontend PR claims backend readiness, verify:

1. Browser configuration uses only the gateway base URL.
2. Browser network traffic contains no requests to service ports `8101` through
   `8106`.
3. CORS preflight succeeds for the frontend origin.
4. Register or login returns `ApiResponse.success` and a JWT.
5. Authenticated requests send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.
6. The browser does not send `X-User-Id`, `X-Username`, `X-User-Role`, or
   `X-Internal-Token`.
7. Product list, product detail, and inventory detail use gateway paths.
8. Order creation uses a unique `idempotencyKey` per checkout attempt.
9. Payment uses a unique `idempotencyKey` per pay attempt and handles
   `40901`, `40902`, and `40903` as state-refresh cases.
10. Admin and AI pages use `/api/admin/**` gateway paths only.
11. All success and error handling reads `success`, `code`, `message`, and
    `data` from the `ApiResponse` envelope.

The k6 gateway script in `pressure/mini-mall-gateway.js` is the backend-side
smoke target for the gateway contract and should track the canonical paths in
`docs/api-gateway-contract.md`.

heading: Follow-up Task Boundaries
text:
Follow-up Task Boundaries

Task 2 should implement the canonical gateway routes and public auth bypass paths for `/api/users/register` and `/api/users/login`.

Task 3 should verify protected canonical routes, trusted header stripping/injection, rate-limit errors, CORS preflight, and non-exposure of `/internal/**`.

Task 6 and Task 7 should update documentation and browser-like scripts so recommended examples use only canonical paths.

Task 5 records the product status mutation policy: customer product APIs remain read-only, current product write endpoints are not admin-safe without RBAC, and the future admin direction is `PUT /api/admin/products/{productId}/status`.

heading: Decision Summary
text:
Decision Summary

Task 4 should remain split. The DTO and pagination contract work crosses common-core plus user, product, inventory, order, and payment service boundaries.

Pagination decision: move `PageResponse` to `common-core` in Task 4.2. The same response shape is now duplicated in product-service and order-service, so keeping service-local copies would create two public pagination contracts.

Identifier rule: public customer DTOs should use named business identifiers such as `userId`, `productId`, `orderNo`, and `paymentNo`. They should not expose a naked `id` field. Internal service-to-service DTOs may remain separate as long as they are not routed through api-gateway as browser contracts.

Enum rule: public status-like fields should serialize as enum strings. Current controller tests already assert strings such as `ON_SHELF`, `IN_STOCK`, `PENDING_PAYMENT`, and `SUCCESS` in several places.

heading: Pagination Findings
text:
Pagination Findings

The public pagination shape is already consistent at the JSON field level:

| Field | Meaning | Current copies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | Page content array | `product-service` and `order-service` |
| `page` | Zero-based page number | `product-service` and `order-service` |
| `size` | Requested page size | `product-service` and `order-service` |
| `totalElements` | Total matching records | `product-service` and `order-service` |
| `totalPages` | Total pages | `product-service` and `order-service` |

The implementation gap is ownership, not shape. Both `product-service/src/main/java/com/minimall/product/dto/PageResponse.java` and `order-service/src/main/java/com/minimall/order/dto/PageResponse.java` define the same public contract. Task 4.2 should add `com.minimall.common.core.response.PageResponse` and remove the duplicate service-local records.

5. 每个页面的关键交互状态

| 页面 | 关键交互状态 |
| --- | --- |
| 登录 | 表单校验（用户名 / 密码非空）；按钮 loading；成功跳 redirect 或 `/products`；失败展示后端 message；401 不崩溃；入口"去注册" |
| 注册 | 校验（用户名非空、密码 ≥6 位对齐后端、email 非空时合法、phone ≤32）；按钮 loading；成功提示后跳 `/login`；失败展示 message |
| 商品列表 | loading（骨架）/ empty（无商品）/ error（重试）；状态筛选切换；下架商品弱化（灰标 + 弱化入口）；分页切换；点击进详情 |
| 商品详情 | 商品 + 库存并行加载；商品不存在→error；下架禁用下单；库存不足 / OUT_OF_STOCK / INACTIVE 禁用下单；数量受库存上限约束；未登录点下单→跳 `/login?redirect=` |
| 下单确认 | 进页生成 idempotencyKey；商品 / 库存复查；下架或缺货禁止确认；按钮 loading 防重复点击；成功跳 `/orders/{orderNo}`；失败恢复按钮 |
| 我的订单 | 未登录→跳登录；loading / empty / error；按状态显示操作（待支付→去支付 / 取消；其它→查看详情）；取消需 ConfirmDialog，成功刷新列表；分页 |
| 订单详情 | 未登录→跳登录；不存在 / 无权→404 文案（后端越权返 404）；按状态显操作（PENDING_PAYMENT→去支付 / 取消；PAID→查看支付信息）；取消 / 支付后重拉详情 |

heading: 一、总体评价（真实）
text:
一、总体评价（真实）

后端契约整体**干净、自洽、边界清晰**，适合前端直接对接：

- 所有公开 REST 均通过 `ApiResponse<T>{success, code, message, data}` 统一封装（`common-core/.../response/ApiResponse.java`）。
- 分页统一为 `PageResponse<T>{content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages}`，0-based。
- 网关与下游服务**共用同一套 `ErrorCode` 枚举**，错误响应格式一致，不会出现两套错误体。
- 安全边界已落地：网关剥离浏览器传入的 `X-User-Id/X-Username` 并从 JWT 注入可信值；`/internal/**` 在网关被显式拒绝。
- 状态字段全部使用枚举，业务异常走 `BusinessException`，符合后端硬规则。

**任务树合理**：`validate-dependencies` 通过（10 任务、26 依赖、0 无效），拓扑正确（脚手架 → API client → 路由/认证 → 各页面 → 验收），task 2（API client）为关键瓶颈，符合工程直觉。

**主要风险集中在"文档表述与代码实现的细节偏差"**，而非后端缺陷。其中 1 个为高优先（订单数据结构），其余为中/低。下面逐条列出，**全部已用源码核实**。

---

heading: 用户 `/api/users/**`
text:
用户 `/api/users/**`

- `POST /register` 入参校验（`RegisterRequest`）：`username` 非空 ≤64；`password` **最少 6 位** ≤128；`email` 可空，但**非空时必须是合法邮箱** ≤128；`phone` 可空 ≤32。
- `POST /register` 返回（`UserResponse`）：`userId, username, email, phone, status`（`status` ∈ `ACTIVE|DISABLED`）。
- `POST /login` 返回（`LoginResponse`）：`token, tokenType("Bearer"), userId, username` —— **登录响应已含 userId/username，可直接初始化 currentUser，无需强制再调 /me**。
- `GET /me` 返回（`CurrentUserResponse`）：**仅 `userId, username`**（无 email/phone）。

heading: 库存 `/api/inventories/**`
text:
库存 `/api/inventories/**`

- `GET /{productId}` 返回（`InventoryResponse`）：`productId, availableStock(int), lockedStock(int), stockState`（`IN_STOCK|OUT_OF_STOCK|INACTIVE`）。

heading: 网关 / 错误码 / 安全（已核实）
text:
网关 / 错误码 / 安全（已核实）

- 错误码为**数字字符串**：`SUCCESS=0, BAD_REQUEST=40000, VALIDATION_ERROR=40001, UNAUTHORIZED=40100, FORBIDDEN=40300, NOT_FOUND=40400, CONFLICT=40900, ORDER_CANCELLED=40901, ORDER_INVALID_STATE=40902, PAYMENT_ALREADY_SUCCESS=40903, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS=42900, INTERNAL_ERROR=50000`。
- 网关 401/403/429 通过 `GatewayErrorResponseWriter` 使用**同一 ErrorCode 枚举**输出，即线上 wire `code` 是 `"40100"/"40300"/"42900"`，**不是** `"UNAUTHORIZED"` 这类名字（文档散文里用的是枚举名）。
- 网关端口 `8080`（`API_GATEWAY_PORT`）。CORS 允许 `http://localhost:*` 与 `http://127.0.0.1:*`、方法含 OPTIONS、**`allow_credentials=false`**。限流：令牌桶 replenish 10/s、burst 20、fail-open。

---

heading: R2（中）错误码 wire 值是数字，不是枚举名
text:
R2（中）错误码 wire 值是数字，不是枚举名

契约散文写 `UNAUTHORIZED/TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`，但 JSON `code` 实际是 `"40100"/"42900"`。
- 建议：API client 的拦截器**优先按 HTTP 状态码**（401/403/429/404/409/500）分流，`ApiResponse.code` 作为细分（如 40901/40902/40903 支付状态刷新）。不要去匹配字符串枚举名。

heading: R4（中）未支付订单查支付详情会返回 404
text:
R4（中）未支付订单查支付详情会返回 404

`PaymentQueryService`：无支付记录 → `NOT_FOUND(40400)`。PENDING 订单从未支付时 `GET /api/payments/{orderNo}` 会 404。
- 建议：订单详情页/支付页拉取支付信息时，把 404 当作"暂无支付信息"的空状态处理，**不要弹全局错误**，更不能因此判定订单异常。

heading: R6（低）`/me` 字段精简
text:
R6（低）`/me` 字段精简

`/me` 只有 `userId/username`，无 email/phone；登录响应也无 email/phone（只有注册响应有）。
- 建议：authStore.currentUser 仅建模 `userId/username`，不要在导航栏/资料处期望 email/phone。

heading: R8（低）金额为 BigDecimal
text:
R8（低）金额为 BigDecimal

`price/totalAmount/unitPrice/amount` 是 BigDecimal，JSON 序列化为数字。
- 建议：展示用固定两位（如 `toFixed(2)` 或 Intl 货币格式），避免浮点显示问题；不要参与不必要的前端数值运算。

heading: 四、已对齐决策（2026-05-21 确认）
text:
四、已对齐决策（2026-05-21 确认）

> 以下为与负责人对齐后的最终口径，后续任务以此为准。

1. **环境变量名**：统一用 `VITE_API_BASE_URL`，默认 `http://localhost:8080`；该名称也已同步到 `docs/frontend-integration.md`。
2. **商品列表搜索**：**不做**。后端无 keyword，Phase 1 不实现搜索框（含本地过滤），避免无效请求。
3. **商品列表状态展示**：**全部展示并弱化下架**。列表拉取全部状态（不强制 `status=ON_SHELF`）；`OFF_SHELF` 商品打灰色"已下架"标签、弱化购买入口；详情页对下架商品禁用下单。（对应 R3，按 PRD 6.4 描述实现。）
4. **后端文档修订**：`docs/frontend-integration.md` 的订单示例（扁平 → `items[]`）与错误码 wire 值说明，**放进 Task #12（文档与验收）一并更正**，本阶段不单独改。
5. **`/403` 页面定位**：**保留作兜底**。订单越权返回 404，统一渲染为"订单不存在或无权访问"；`/403` 仅兜底网关 FORBIDDEN(40300)，不围绕它设计鉴权 UX。
6. **登录后初始化用户**：**登录直接用响应中的 userId/username 初始化 currentUser**（省一次请求）；页面刷新/恢复 token 时再调 `GET /api/users/me` 校验有效性，失效则清 token 跳登录。

heading: MiniMall Phase 1 — Customer Frontend UI/UX Redesign Brief
text:
MiniMall Phase 1 — Customer Frontend UI/UX Redesign Brief

> **Status:** Design contract (not yet implemented).
> **Scope:** Visual & interaction overhaul of the existing customer frontend.
> **Hard boundaries:** No new business modules. No API contract changes. No backend changes. No new product fields. No admin/RBAC/cart/address/coupon/real-payment/refund.
> **Owner directive:** "PRD decides feature boundaries; visual expression is yours to drive. You may aggressively improve UI, but cannot add business modules."

This document is **self-binding**: during implementation I MUST honor the rules in §10. If a step tempts me to "just override Element Plus colors", that step is wrong — re-read §0 and §10.

---

heading: 1. Design intent
text:
1. Design intent

**Style name:** *Soft Minimal Storefront* — boutique DTC voice, restrained, breathing, slightly warm. Reference vibe: Apple Store product pages, Aesop, Everlane, Stripe Checkout.

**Voice keywords:** quiet, considered, deliberate whitespace, ink + paper, product imagery carries the color, motion is gentle and brief.

**One-sentence test:** if a casual visitor cannot tell within 1 second that this is a *shop* and not a *dashboard*, the design has failed.

---

heading: 2.2 Type
text:
2.2 Type

| Token | Family / weight / size / line-height | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `display-xl` | Inter Tight / 700 / 48 / 1.1, letter-spacing -0.02em | Login hero, payment amount, 404 numeral |
| `display` | Inter Tight / 600 / 32 / 1.15 | Product list headline, payment success title |
| `h1` | Inter / 600 / 24 / 1.3 | Page titles |
| `h2` | Inter / 600 / 18 / 1.4 | Section titles inside pages |
| `body` | Inter / 400 / 14 / 1.7 | Paragraphs, descriptions |
| `body-strong` | Inter / 500 / 14 / 1.6 | Inline labels |
| `caption` | Inter / 400 / 12 / 1.5 | Meta, order time, hints |
| `mono-sm` | ui-monospace / 400 / 12 / 1.5 | Order numbers, product IDs |
| `price-lg` | Inter / 700 / 32 / 1, tabular-nums | Detail page price |
| `price-md` | Inter / 600 / 20 / 1, tabular-nums | List & order card price |
| `amount-display` | Inter Tight / 700 / 56 / 1, tabular-nums | Payment page amount block |
| `brand` | Inter Tight / 600 / 18, letter-spacing +0.04em | "MiniMall" wordmark |

**zh fallback:** `"PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB", "Microsoft YaHei", sans-serif` after the Inter family.

**Decision:** Numerals use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` everywhere money or counts appear, so columns of prices and order totals align cleanly.

heading: 3.1 Keep vs replace (storefront surface)
text:
3.1 Keep vs replace (storefront surface)

| Surface | Decision |
|---|---|
| `el-form` / `el-form-item` validation engine | **Keep** (form rules work well, no visual chrome on the user) |
| `ElMessage` toast | **Keep** (top-right, brief, neutral) |
| `ElMessageBox.confirm` (cancel order dialog) | **Keep** (modal chrome is fine; restyle text only) |
| `el-input` (under the hood) | **Wrap** inside our own `<Field>` so the visible shell is ours |
| `el-button` | **Replace** with `<Button variant="primary | ghost | text">` |
| `el-tag` | **Replace** with `<Pill>` and `<DotStatus>` |
| `el-result` | **Replace** with `<EmptyState>` / `<ErrorState>` |
| `el-empty` | **Replace** with `<EmptyState>` |
| `el-alert` | **Replace** with `<Notice>` (hairline-bordered, no harsh fill) |
| `el-loading` directive | **Remove**. Replace with skeleton components per page |
| `el-pagination` | **Replace** with `<Pager>` (text-link prev/next + page chips) |
| `el-input-number` | **Replace** with `<QuantityStepper>` |
| `el-select` | **Replace** on storefront filters with `<PillGroup>` tab pills |
| `el-divider` | **Replace** with `<Hairline />` (1px `--ink-100`) |
| `el-row` / `el-col` grid | **Replace** with CSS grid (`.grid-cols-*` utility classes) |

heading: 3.3 Molecule components (new)
text:
3.3 Molecule components (new)

```
<AppHeader />            // brand + nav + account chip, scroll-aware
<AppFooter />            // quiet brand line at canvas color
<PageContainer width="xs | sm | md | lg | xl">
<ProductCover :productId :name :size :variant?="0|1|2|3" />

```

heading: 4. Product cover system (no-backend-image strategy)
text:
4. Product cover system (no-backend-image strategy)

The single most important visual lever. Must look intentional, not "placeholder". Used on: list card, detail hero, detail variant thumbnails, checkout item row, order card, order detail row, payment receipt mini-thumb.

heading: 4.2 Palette set (8 boutique palettes)
text:
4.2 Palette set (8 boutique palettes)

Each palette is a 2-stop gradient. Hand-tuned to read as boutique product photography, never neon.

```
P0  Sand          #E9DECE → #C8B8A2
P1  Olive         #D2D4B6 → #97A07A
P2  Slate         #C3CCD3 → #7E8A93
P3  Clay          #E7C9B2 → #B58A6F
P4  Moss          #C7D2BD → #7D8C70
P5  Smoke         #DCDADA → #9A9695
P6  Linen         #EBE2D6 → #C3B59E
P7  Mist          #CFD7DC → #8E99A1
```

All palettes are low-chroma. No saturated colors. The product list's overall color impression should feel like a stack of folded fabrics.

heading: 4.5 Aspect ratios by placement
text:

| Placement | AR | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| List card | **4:5** | Taller than square; boutique vertical feel |
| Detail hero | **4:5** | Same AR, larger; "detail-grade" rendering (see 4.6) |
| Detail variant thumbnails (×3) | 1:1 | Decorative, swap hero on click (re-seed geometry) |
| Checkout item row | 1:1, 80px | Compact |
| Order card | 1:1, 64px | Compact |
| Order detail item row | 1:1, 72px | Slightly larger than list |
| Payment receipt mini-thumb | 1:1, 48px | Smallest |

heading: 4.7 Variant thumbnails (decorative, ≤3)
text:
4.7 Variant thumbnails (decorative, ≤3)

- Below the hero, three 56×56 thumbnails, 1:1.
- Each uses the same palette but a *different* geometry index (`(geometryIdx+1) % 6`, `+2`, `+3`).
- Clicking a thumbnail swaps the hero's geometry with a 220ms cross-fade. **No business meaning** — this is a delight detail to make the detail page feel like a proper product page. Tracked as visual only; never wired to inventory or API.

5. Page-by-page specification

Container widths are **page-specific** by design:

| Page | Max width |
